baseline_models.mechanism: The speakers publicly demand a temporal coordinate for a stated commitment, then make correspondence between speech and realization the test of the speakers' truthfulness.

activation_trace.role: Vocalized speech makes the timing challenge a public utterance.
A promise opens expectation while binding the utterance to a future outcome.
Occurrence in time supplies the condition under which the claim can be checked.
Truth as agreement of speech with reality supplies the challengers' stated criterion.

changed_reading.before: A bare request for the date of a future event.
changed_reading.after: A public credibility test: name when the committed event will occur so speech can be checked against reality.

baseline_models.mechanism: The packet's non-dominant mappings of the promise root activate counted, recurring time and the yearly cycle; joined to متى, the promise is treated as a schedule that the challengers want made numerically auditable.

activation_trace.role: Counted and recurring time turns the promise into a proposed timetable.
The year-cycle gives that timetable a calendrical scale.
Actual occurrence would terminate the count and expose the schedule to inspection.
Fulfilment in action makes arrival at the proposed time the audit condition.

changed_reading.before: Tell us generally when the promise will happen.
changed_reading.after: State the count or calendar by which this promise can be audited as fulfilled.

context_deltas.mechanism: The earlier denial of the Hour's arrival is answered by emphatic arrival, while hiddenness is paired with exhaustive non-absence and an obligating record. The timing question therefore tests whether an unseen event can be trusted before it arrives visibly, not merely whether a date exists.

activation_trace.role: The appointed aspect of the promise anchors the demand for a time.
Realization of the promise anchors truth in eventual performance.
Denied and emphatically asserted coming supplies the contested arrival mechanism.
Concealment from sight explains why the promised arrival is not presently inspectable.
Negated distance, absence, and escape block the inference that hidden means missed.
A record that fixes an obligating determination supplies stability before visible arrival.

structural_cues: 34:3 directly opposes لا تأتينا الساعة to the emphatic لتأتينكم.
The temporal ساعة at 34:3 is retained structurally because the supplied س و ع branches do not support that sense.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies denied arrival, assured arrival, concealment, exhaustive non-absence, and a fixed record; I infer that the challenge converts lack of present visibility into a truth objection. A live alternative is a sincere request for chronology.

changed_reading.before: The question asks for missing chronological information.
changed_reading.after: The question voices refusal to credit an appointed but unseen arrival, even though hiddenness does not entail absence or escape.

context_deltas.mechanism: The death in 34:14 has already occurred while a supported structure remains standing; hidden creeping consumption eventually produces collapse, and only collapse produces recognition. This separates the time an event becomes true from the time observers can detect it.

activation_trace.role: Being or occurring in time anchors the distinction between event-time and observation-time.
Fulfilment can be real before witnesses recognize that it has been fulfilled.
Hidden creeping supplies an imperceptible process between occurrence and disclosure.
Progressive consumption and decay remove the support without an announced deadline.
Noisy collapse is the delayed visible signal, not the beginning of the underlying event.
Disclosure follows collapse and marks the observers' recognition-time.

structural_cues: In 34:14 death is decreed before the creature consumes the staff, the body falls, and the jinn finally know.
The repeated فلما clauses expose a sequence rather than a single simultaneous moment.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies prior death, hidden erosion, collapse, and subsequent disclosure; I infer two clocks, occurrence and recognition. A live alternative is that the episode illustrates hidden knowledge without defining the promise's timing.

changed_reading.before: When will the promised event begin?
changed_reading.after: Which time is being demanded: the event's real occurrence or the later collapse by which observers finally recognize it?

context_deltas.mechanism: In 34:20 an expectation becomes verified through people's following, yet 34:21 denies coercive authority and makes the result discriminative. Truth is thus not only prediction matched by an external event; conduct can realize an expectation and reveal affiliation.

activation_trace.role: Truth as fulfilment anchors the challenge in realized rather than merely asserted content.
An expectation verified in action supplies a behavioral mode of becoming true.
An initially uncertain expectation supplies what subsequent conduct verifies.
Following supplies the human action that materially realizes the expectation.
The negation of overpowering force keeps realization from being reduced to compulsion.
Interpenetrating doubt supplies the contrasting state that the enacted test exposes.

structural_cues: 34:20 excepts a believing group from the following.
34:21 explicitly frames the absence of سلطان around distinguishing belief from doubt.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies an expectation verified by following, an exception, and no coercive force; I infer that behavior helps realize and disclose the forecast. A live alternative is that this mechanism belongs only to the Iblis episode.

changed_reading.before: If you are truthful means only that your forecast must later match an external event.
changed_reading.after: If you are truthful also becomes a behavioral sorting challenge: present following or refusal can realize expectations and disclose allegiance before the final event.

context_deltas.mechanism: Calibrated months and measured travel make a counted timetable imaginable, but 34:30 answers the challenge with an appointed day whose boundary cannot move backward or forward. The response supplies invariance rather than the requested date.

activation_trace.role: Counted recurring time frames the challengers' demand as a schedule audit.
The annual cycle broadens the possible calendar on which they seek a coordinate.
Two explicitly known lunar months model movement converted into calendar units.
Measured planning of travel supplies the surah's concrete schedule-making analogue.
The promise becomes an appointment bounded by a specific temporal locus.
A delimited duration gives the appointment its day-scale.
Negated postponement fixes the appointment's rear boundary.
Negated advance fixes the appointment's front boundary.

structural_cues: 34:12 quantifies morning and evening movement by months, and 34:18 measures travel by nights and days.
34:30 uses ساعة to deny even minimal temporal movement; it remains structural because the packet's س و ع inventory lacks a temporal branch.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies calibrated travel, an appointed day, and symmetric denial of delay and advance; I infer that the question seeks a movable human-style timetable while the answer asserts a fixed but undisclosed boundary. The simpler alternative is merely that the date is unknown to the challengers.

changed_reading.before: Give the numerical date so the promise can be checked.
changed_reading.after: The promise has an exact, non-negotiable boundary, but truthfulness is answered by its invariance rather than by yielding its calendar coordinate.

context_deltas.mechanism: Repeated speech returns among social ranks in 34:31-33, while 34:46 prescribes standing singly and in pairs to reflect. The plural timing challenge can therefore function as a circulating group refrain whose social momentum is interrupted by smaller units of deliberation.

activation_trace.role: Speech circulating among people lets the plural question operate as a repeated public refrain.
Back-and-forth speech turns saying into a negotiated dispute between social parties.
Separation into one breaks the collective speech unit.
Joining one to one supplies the smallest dialogical check on the refrain.
Solitary standing removes the shelter of collective repetition.
Sustained inward deliberation replaces reflexive public repetition.

structural_cues: 34:31-33 repeatedly stage the weak and arrogant returning speech and blame to one another.
34:46 shifts explicitly from a collective audience to pairs and individuals before reflection.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a plural refrain, recursive social dialogue, and a one-or-two-person reflective counter-form; I infer that group circulation helps sustain the timing challenge. A live alternative is that the plural is only ordinary collective grammar.

changed_reading.before: Several people independently ask the same chronological question.
changed_reading.after: They voice a socially reproduced challenge whose force depends on circulation, and whose grip may weaken when the group is decomposed into reflective pairs and individuals.

context_deltas.mechanism: The prospective day of gathering in 34:40 becomes اليوم in 34:42, after which mutual benefit and harm are unavailable. The promised future is a deictic threshold: once crossed, the question's distant 'when' becomes an immediate 'today' with altered agency.

activation_trace.role: An appointment anchors the future temporal point whose deixis will reverse.
A prospective span of time establishes the not-yet day.
Driving and gathering the group supplies the event that crosses the threshold.
Joining the dispersed makes the promised day a collective present.
The same temporal scale is now named as today, completing the deictic reversal.
Negated benefit marks the loss of prior interpersonal agency after the threshold.
Negated harm completes the suspension of mutual control on that day.

structural_cues: 34:40 opens prospectively with ويوم, whereas 34:42 opens from inside the event with فاليوم.
The shift follows gathering and precedes the verdict addressed to deniers.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies a future day, gathering, then an explicit today with changed capacities; I infer a deictic threshold rather than a mere date. A live alternative is ordinary narrative sequencing.

changed_reading.before: When will that future date arrive?
changed_reading.after: When will the temporal viewpoint flip, making the distant promised day this present day and ending the agency available before it?

context_deltas.mechanism: The closing sequence moves from no escape and seizure from a near place to failed reaching from a far place and finally a barrier between people and desire. The appointment is therefore also a deadline of accessibility: after it, belated assent cannot reach back across the new separation.

activation_trace.role: The appointment anchors a boundary with a before and an after.
Occurrence marks the transition at which available action changes.
Failure of escape or attainment removes the possibility of outrunning the boundary.
Seizure converts the promised time into an enforced capture point.
Place derived from being gives the capture a near spatial coordinate.
Nearness makes capture immediate rather than remotely avoidable.
The interrogative reach of 'how or whence' mirrors the focus question after the boundary has passed.
The alternative mapping to season or due time activates the missed temporal opportunity.
Stretching to take and reach supplies the failed attempt at belated access.
A second place-coordinate locates the attempted reach on the far side of the boundary.
Distance blocks access to what is acknowledged too late.
An intervening barrier makes the loss of access explicit.
The interval between parties and objects of desire becomes an impassable middle.
Desire names what remains wanted but no longer reachable.

structural_cues: 34:51 combines no escape with taking from a near place; 34:52 answers belated belief with failed reach from a far place.
34:54 closes the surah by placing a barrier between them and what they desire.
context_deltas.reader_inference: The packet supplies near capture, no escape, failed reaching from afar, and a final barrier; I infer that the appointment closes a window for effective response. A live alternative is that the spatial sequence only describes consequences after judgment.

changed_reading.before: When will the promised event occur?
changed_reading.after: Until when does effective response remain reachable before the appointed event turns time into an uncrossable separation?

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is surprising because it uses the packet's form-distant ق و ل to ق ل ل mapping rather than the ordinary lexical sense of يقولون. It remains anchored to the supplied focus inventory and coherently models the question as rhetorical diminishment; downstream prose should mark it as a branch-induced 'as if' effect, not translate يقولون as making little.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: The split inventory attached to يقولون at word 1.

activation_trace.role: Smallness and diminution recast the utterance as an attempt to belittle a delayed promise.
Instability and agitation make repeated timing demands a way of trying to unsettle the promise's standing.

changed_reading.before: They utter a timing question about the promise.
changed_reading.after: Their utterance acts as if it could make the promise small or unstable by measuring its credibility against immediate arrival.

surprising_valid_outliers.containment: This is a cross-domain spatial reading because it projects the later mechanics of casting onto the focus verb of saying. It remains valid as an exploratory model because the focus utterance targets an unseen future appointment and 34:48/53 explicitly contrast casting truth with casting speech at the unseen from afar; downstream prose should use 'behaves like' rather than claim lexical identity.
surprising_valid_outliers.focus_anchor: يقولون متى directs speech toward the unseen time of الوعد.

activation_trace.role: An outward utterance supplies the verbal object that can be spatially modeled as cast.
The unseen appointment supplies the distant target of the utterance.
Casting truth supplies forceful directed projection from the side that knows.
Reality-stable truth identifies what is projected with warranted force.
The concealed domain marks the target as unavailable to ordinary sight.
Casting speech or fault supplies the opposing act of verbal projection without access.
The unseen is explicitly the domain at which that speech is thrown.
Distance explains the challengers' lack of epistemic contact with the future they target.

changed_reading.before: They ask for information about an unknown future date.
changed_reading.after: Their timing challenge behaves like speech thrown at the unseen from a distant epistemic position, contrasted with truth cast from knowledge.

strongest_changes: The staff episode separates real occurrence from delayed human recognition, destabilizing the assumption that an event begins only when observers see it.
The explicit answer turns a requested date into a fixed but undisclosed appointment whose boundary cannot be advanced or postponed.
The closing near/far/barrier sequence recasts the promise as the deadline after which effective response is no longer reachable.
Repeated social speech and the one-or-pair reflection instruction make the plural question readable as a circulating refrain rather than isolated inquiry.
summary.what_was_special: Whole-surah activation made timing material, spatial, and social: hidden decay delays disclosure, calibrated travel evokes schedules, future day becomes present today, collective speech is decomposed for reflection, and late belief fails to reach across a barrier. The split focus mappings additionally exposed counted-year and minimization readings that a conservative synthesis would likely suppress.
remaining_uncertainties: Whether the counted-year activation from the split promise mapping should enter final prose or remain an exploratory audit note.
Whether the occurrence-versus-recognition distinction in 34:14 is a governing analogy for the promise or only a local illustration of hidden knowledge.
Whether the plural يقولون carries a socially reproduced refrain beyond ordinary collective grammar.
Whether speech-casting at the unseen is structurally intended or only a productive cross-domain echo.
